description: Module aim:

This module aims to equip student nurses with complimentary underpinning pathophysiological knowledge to enhance nursing practice and to support the development of future clinical assessment and diagnostic knowledge at Level M.
Content:

Students will review the genome and genetic variations: chromosome number and structure, changes in DNA sequence and copy number variation, genes and protein function, polymorphism. Multifactorial genetic conditions, single-gene conditions, chromosomal conditions, mitochondrial conditions. Cellular biology and the processes of inflammatory/infectious responses, cancer and cancerous metastases.

The study of pathophysiological variation in all body systems. When exploring systems, students will consider these pathophysiological variations across the lifespan and provide explanation and rationale for the use of common diagnostic mechanisms and measures.
Strategies:

Study of the cell, cellular changes and genomics will be developed through a lecture series with directed pre and post online activities and reading and workshop activities. Through directed group seminar work students will explore in depth patho-physiological changes in a given system and will present this learning to the whole group. Seminars will be recorded via lecture capture software (Panopto) and will include formative feedback made available to the whole group.

outcomes.outcome: Demonstrate in depth understanding of the mechanisms leading to cell changes, cell injury and cell death (Examination)
Explain how alterations to the genome influence individual health and pathophysiological processes. (Examination)
Compare variations in pathophysiological processes across the human lifespan (Examination)
Synthesise and communicate complex ideas and pathophysiological processes of common and acute conditions experienced by people. (Examination)

description: This module is designed to enable students to analyse and synthesise detailed knowledge of altered health conditions to safely respond to deteriorating patients. Students will interpret a range of results to formulate a defendable condition hypothesis (working diagnosis). Furthermore, students will critically analyse the potential chronic condition and pharmacological effects on acutely ill service users. Using these results students will independently articulate clinical management decisions developing an appropriate plan of adult nursing care including safe delegation or referral to medical staff or other appropriate professionals.

The module will develop knowledge of prescribing legislation, and application of detailed pharmacological knowledge to adult nursing. Bioscience concepts will be developed as a core component to support students with their clinical decision-making.

A range of learning and teaching activities will be used, including case studies, lead lectures, group work seminars, and skills and simulation teaching, supported by digital learning and engagement with service users, other agencies, and professionals, as appropriate. Any outstanding communication and management skills or nursing procedures will be assessed through simulation during this module with the involvement of appropriate practice assessors.

Utilise bioscience knowledge to critically analyse and evaluate clinical information in order to interpret physiological deterioration in a service user with comorbidities and acute complex conditions.

description: This module aligns to NMC (2019) Standards of Proficiency for Midwives Domain 1, and 5 and promotes professional excellence in practice and a personal commitment to global midwifery aims for safe and enriching care for women and communities served by midwives. Learners will critically evaluate the ways in which enhancement and advancement of midwifery practice can benefit individual woman and childbearing people, their partners, wider families, and newborn infants. The module will develop strengths-based approaches and explore success as a midwife through reflection on personal strengths and professional career planning, capitalising on interest and intent. Professional regulatory, legal and ethical theories and frameworks, as well as contemporary contexts for practice will be critically reviewed against midwifery specialist, leadership and managerial roles. Learners will explore the challenges of being an autonomous practitioner, expert, leader and member of interdisciplinary and multiagency teams where common goals are shared and when philosophies for care do not align and how they can effectively promote human rights approaches to care as a midwife working across a range of professional groups, services and contexts. Using enquiry-based learning, learners will be expected to independently identify research questions and to demonstrate discernment in the location and application of evidence to inform learning.

description: The module aligns to NMC (2019) Standards of Proficiency for Midwives Domain 4 and will introduce learners to key concepts, policy, and professional, ethical, and legal practice related to caring for women, childbearing people and newborn infants with complications and additional needs. This includes understanding how to work effectively in partnership with those requiring additional care, as well as the role of the midwife as a colleague within inter-disciplinary, multi-disciplinary and multi-agency teams. Learners will develop their knowledge of anatomy, physiology and pathophysiology related to pre-existing and emerging conditions and will consider other key factors that may necessitate additional care to optimise outcomes. Skills in identifying, assessing, planning, implementing and evaluating care will be examined to include first line management, referral and follow up and some emergency situations. Learners will continue to progress their research and application skills through enquiry-based learning and will reflect on their performance and identify their own development needs to optimise their impact as aspiring midwives.

Locate, critique, evaluate and apply a range of evidence to inform the assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation of care and support plans for women, childbearing people and newborn infants with additional care needs
Using a reflection-in-action approach, self-reflect on professional development needs and formulate an action plan to address this

data.title: LI Research in Professional Practice
data.restrictions: Students must have completed year one of BNurs/MNurs
description: Aim:

To enable the student to apply developing knowledge of research and the nursing evidence base to the development of practice and the delivery of improvement and on-going change. To consider research and professional development within the context of the relevant legal, ethical and professional frameworks underpinning research governance and safe professional practice.
Content:
1. Students will explore research paradigms and process in nursing , common research methods and approaches underpinning research within healthcare.

2. Students will be introduced to research governance, ethics and other legal, professional and ethical concepts and frameworks (e.g beneficence, duty of candour, accountability, equality) that frame both research and professional practice.

3. Students will be introduced to the role of research and audit in care quality improvement and explore some of the factors associated with implementing knowledge in practice together with change management. Measures of quality: performance indicators, standards and benchmarks

4. Professional self-regulation. Revalidation.  Critical reflection, gaining and using feedback (self, peer, service user, employer/mentor).Adult learning theories, theories of motivation, lifelong learning and the learning organization.
Learning and Teaching strategy:

A blended approach will be used throughout. Lectures ( some online) will support the development of critiquing skills in group research workshops and seminars. Group tutorials will support students in the development of their poster.

outcomes.outcome: Demonstrate an understanding of ethical, legal and professional frameworks underpinning research governance, professional conduct and the delivery of equitable care (Essay Assignment)
Discuss how nursing research, improvement science and theories of change inform quality and practice development in nursing (Essay assignment)
Consider different approaches to research in developing knowledge and evidence for practice (Group Poster presentation)
Disseminate evidence based knowledge that facilitates learning for peer groups (Group Poster presentation)

description: This module aligns to NMC (2019) Standards of Proficiency for Midwives Domain 2 and 5 and will develop learners critical understanding and application of the concepts, principles, frameworks and factors that support effective midwifery continuity of care(r). Learners will develop their professional understanding of advocacy that promotes and delivers positive outcomes and the professional and interpersonal skills required to enact this. description: Aims
This module aims to enable students to:
Develop a critical understanding of altered health occurring in common conditions and symptoms across the adult lifespan;

Develop knowledge of pharmacology, pharmacokinetics and therapeutics of common medicines and the ability to identify differences in pharmacology raised by factors such as age, weight, route and concordance;
Undertake shared assessments and shared decision-making and facilitate transition from service to service or between care settings;
Develop further in-depth knowledge of field specific strengths-based, therapeutic adult nursing related to commonly occurring conditions;
Evaluate the effectiveness of person centred evidence-based care prioritisation and planning.
Content:

Commonly encountered physical conditions including cardiovascular, endocrine, genetic, immune, infection, gastrointestinal, haematological, hepatic, musculoskeletal, neurological, oncological, renal, respiratory systems. Visual and auditory conditions.

Commonly encountered mental health conditions - mental distress and anxiety, depression, self-harm and suicidal ideation, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, personality disorders, addiction and substance misuse.

Nursing children, young people and adults with learning disabilities ? including approaches to reasonable adjustments, medication management, empowerment, independence and inclusion in therapeutic management.This module aims to enable students to systematically apply knowledge of therapeutic nursing practice to the care of individuals with altered health and commonly occurring conditions within a field of practice. As part of this students will consider the impact of pharmacokinetics and pharmacotherapeutics within their field of practice. Students will critically evaluate the effectiveness of person centred evidence-based therapeutic nursing care including the safe person centred transition of care for people across a care pathway and/or integrated health and social care service.

The module will include scenarios to develop learning of assessment and observation for those at risk of deterioration in adults within the context of community, medical and surgical care settings, including the need to base therapeutic interventions on individual needs and preferences and the application of evidence.
Pharmacology and medicine optimisation will be discussed in relation to common conditions. Use of British National Formulary.
Learning and Teaching

A range of learning and teaching activities will be used, including lead lectures, digital learning packages, tutorials, case studies, involvement of service users, other agencies and professionals, as appropriate.

Discuss the principles of shared assessment and shared decision-making in supporting holistic person-centred care;
Using an evidence-based approach, defend the prioritisation of decisions made in the delivery of holistic person centred care for adults;

description: Advanced Clinical Practice Portfolio (Year 1) is a non-credit bearing mandatory module within the MSc Advanced Clinical Practice which will facilitate the professional requirements of a portfolio record of academic and clinical achievements required by the Apprenticeship Standards for Advanced Clinical Practice (2018) and the Multi-professional Framework for ACP (HEE, 2017).

The module will promote the formal evidencing of work- based learning supporting the competencies outlined within the 4 pillars for advanced clinical practice (clinical practice, research, leadership and management and education) combined with the theoretical underpinning delivered via the Masters level preparation.

The learning and teaching approaches will facilitate the compilation of robust evidence to support the individual competencies outlined within the 4 pillars of advanced practice, with work-based sign off of competencies from a designated clinical assessor.

outcomes.outcome: Demonstrate synthesis and application of theoretical content acquired from concurrent Masters level studies in year 1 by successful integration of new knowledge and skills into practice, evidenced through development of an ePortfolio of evidence.

Evidence progression in the clinical, leadership, research and education pillars, over the duration of year 1 of the Masters programme, through the sign off of individual competencies relating to the 4 pillars of advanced clinical practice, utilising a taxonomy of achievement scale.

Demonstrate an understanding and synthesis of work-based learning and theoretical underpinning through the successful completion of a mandatory viva voce exploring the 4 pillars of advanced clinical practice through work-based experiences during semester 3 of year 1 of the Masters programme.

summative: Viva voce: exploring mandatory elements of the ePortfolio during the third semester of year 1.

Competency Sign Off: Clinical Assessor sign off of the competencies within ePortfolio in year 1 utilising a taxonomy of achievement to demonstrate progression in first year of study from initial identified level. Supportive evidence will be provided in the form of an ePortfolio.
The viva voce acts as a gateway for progression into year 2 of the Masters programme.
There is a Pass/ Fail element to the gateway which is a mandatory requirement prior to progressing into Year 2 of the Masters programme.
This meets the mandatory requirements of the Apprenticeship Standards for Advanced Clinical Practice (2018).
reassessment: Viva: Students will be given a re viva opportunity
Portfolio Contents: Students will be given a resubmission opportunity following feedback.
Competency Sign Off: Following liaison with clinical assessor a period of revision will be allocated in order to evidence outstanding work-based competencies

data.title: LM Advanced Practice Research Dissertation
data.restrictions:
Compulsory module for MSc Advanced Clinical Practice & MSc Advanced Practice (Global)

Students must have completed all modules in order to progress to this module

Students must take at least one research methodological module which is appropriate to this module. Project Management and Research Governance is a compulsory pre-requisite for the MSc Advanced Clinical Practice. Advanced Practice (Global) students will need to have achieved the `Creating and Applying Evidence? module
description: To demonstrate students? application of advanced practice research knowledge and skills in their current work place.

outcomes.outcome: Plan an research investigation within a clinical area, research unit or educational institution relevant to health and social care.
Review and critically analyse previous literature and current policy in this area to determine / refine and inform the focus and nature of the investigation.
Determine appropriate methods of investigation for the research task; justifying the advanced practice rationale and recognising its limitations.
Collect or review and critically analyse data or information in the relevant subject field.
Interpret the data collected and explain the significance, clinical relevance and implications for service transformation for patient or population benefit.

summative: Each section of the dissertation thesis/research project (Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion) must be passed with at least 50%, although a nominal fail where the grade is at least 40% in one section will be tolerated.  The student must achieve an overall mark of at least 50%.
A formal presentation in the form of a poster or oral presentation will be examined. This will report the project methodology, outputs and potential impact.
reassessment: Failure to achieve an overall average of at least 50% will require the student to improve and resubmit the work.

data.title: LM Advanced Practice Research Project
data.restrictions: Students need consent for service evaluation; DBS check
description: The Research Project module will support the development of a work-based research project in the form of a service evaluation. The focus of the evaluation will be chosen by the students with guidance from the module team, their allocated dissertation supervisor, in agreement with their Practice Assessor. It will be undertaken in either their usual place of work, or an allocated placement area.
The aim of this module is to develop the student's ability to:
Identify areas of practice requiring service evaluation, based upon clinical or service drivers

Systematically identify, critically appraise and synthesise available evidence to support key themes within the service evaluation and identify appropriate best practice criteria within the contemporaneous evidence base
Gain an understanding of service evaluation methodologies and reporting frameworks

Prepare a project report, in the style of a journal publication, to reflect the key outcome of the literature review and evaluation and propose future areas of development to support quality improvement processes within the clinical area

outcomes.outcome: Plan an investigation within a clinical area relevant to health and social care with a focus on service evaluation methodologies.
Review and critically analyse existing evidence, policies, and guidelines in this area to inform the focus and nature of the investigation.
Determine appropriate methods of investigation; justifying the  rationale and recognising its limitations.
Collect, review and interpret the evaluation data and explain the significance, clinical relevance and implications for service transformation for patient or population benefit.
Present the work in the appropriate format for journal publication an oral presentation of findings.

summative: The word count will be based upon the journal style chosen, with a minimum of 3500 words and a maximum of 7000 words.
The student must achieve an overall mark of at least 50%.
The Research Project will be double-marked.

Presentation (30%):A formal presentation, in the form of a poster presentation will be examined, with questions following from an academic panel. This will report the project methodology, outputs and potential impact.
reassessment: Failure to achieve an overall average of at least 50% in either assessment will require the student to improve and resubmit the failed element only.

description: This 20-credit module is a core module for the MSc Advancing Nursing Science programme. Learners will critically analyse and evaluate the principles of advancing nursing science and prepare for their journey on the masters. You will explore the development of nursing knowledge and to promote the integration of nursing philosophies, theories and research with practice. There will be opportunity to critically discuss contemporary issues and critical reflection on how advances in nursing science will influence you personally and professionally. There will be opportunities for collaborative learning and engagement with visiting lecturers, clinical leaders and researchers

The module structure is blended, with academic support to identify and develop an individualised timetable of experiential work-based learning. You will work with the academic team to apply new knowledge and insight to your practice through the production of original and academic evidence of your personal learning

description: This module develops the ability to undertake an accurate, holistic nursing clinical assessment, diagnosis and immediate triage and management of urgent and critical conditions.
Shared learning across fields of practice

You will develop a systematic approach to assessing and examining children and adults who present with an acute or urgent health conditions. You will learn to identify and recognise the presence of red flags and serious signs and symptoms through communication skills and through a range of diagnostic nursing techniques and procedures.
You'll revise communication techniques such as SBAR as needed for urgent escalation, multi-disciplinary handover and delegation of care.
Field specific learning:

Within your field of practice groups you'll consider care for people with urgent and critical care needs as relevant to your field of nursing. Through facilitated enquiry based learning (EBL) groups you will explore a range of commonly occurring urgent and critical conditions together with consent and care management and medication relevant to your field of practice. You'll revise pathology and nursing care related to conditions.

Each EBL group (of 4-6 students) will present a formative evidence based case seminar to peers. In the labs you will develop skills in undertaking a full assessment and history within the context of your field of practice applying relevant NMC (2018) Annexe A and B skills.

outcomes.outcome: Gain consent and systematically perform a holistic clinical assessment of a person presenting for acute and urgent care within the student's designated field of practice
Accurately use routine diagnostic tools and investigations to safely establish urgent care decisions

Conduct a safe medication assessment, demonstrating knowledge of prescribing legislation, prescription generation and recognising the potential effects of a pharmacological intervention on patient presentation within the field of practice
Systematically communicate findings and recommendations to a team member, providing a clear evidence based rationale for immediate care management
Critically reflect upon the application of theory, guidelines and evidence informing clinical assessment and care management for a range of urgent acute conditions within a field of practice

summative: (100%) Objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) : an OSCE simulation of an urgent patient event set in the context of the student's field of nursing practice. The OSCE duration is one hour and includes four oral or written stations.
There is no compensation on this module. All assessment elements must be passed
reassessment: One further OSCE attempt is permitted. A different OSCE scenario is provided.

711D - MSc Nursing (Child) FT

description: Module Aim

This module is the entry module for the student on MSc Nursing with registration as a nurse in adult or mental health or children's nursing. Students will use this module to advance their knowledge of health and nursing care and apply this to their field of practice. At the end of this module, students will be required to demonstrate the level of practice and underpinning knowledge and skills required by the Practice Assessment Document part 1. This will include simulated clinical experiences for maternity and mental health care for adult students.   An academic and practice assessor will be accountable for ensuring that assessment for this module is completed in line with the NMC (2018) Standards for Student Supervision and Assessment.
Introduction to postgraduate study and professional development to include preparation for practice. The module aims to enable the student to:
Critically analyse health and policy drivers for current nursing practice;
Critique policy and contexts in which individual and population health improvement and care is advanced and delivered;
Critically evaluate a strengths-based approach to health promotion and nursing care;
Critically reflect on communication and relationship management skills as part of nursing health promoting, therapeutic and collegial relationships;
Understand the information and communication needs across the life span and for people with sudden or enduring mental health conditions or learning disability;
Support and develop practice using the holistic and fundamental principles of nursing in line with the NMC Code (NMC 2018a) and Standards (NMC, 2018b) and apply these to a field of practice.
Evidence-based procedures to support health and nursing care including the maintenance of:
Safety, dignity, privacy;
Comfort and sleep;
Skin integrity and hygiene;
Mobility;
Nutrition, hydration;
Elimination;
Temperature regulation;
Safe medicines administration;
Respiratory and circulatory assessment;
Person-centred nursing assessment and care planning;
Reasonable adjustments in care assessment and planning.
A nursing practice placement within the chosen field of practice is included in this module and the assessment will use part 1 Practice Assessment Document.
Learning and Teaching Strategies

A range of learning and teaching activities will be used, including lead lectures, seminars, tutorials, case studies, technology enhanced learning. Service users are actively included in the development of appropriate communication scenarios designed to develop both generic and field related communication skills. Students will be able to draw on a range of online resources that enhance prior learning and develop individual learning needs in biological and psychological sciences that underpin fundamental care.

outcomes.outcome: Critically reflect upon the ethical, legal and professional responsibility of the nurse in using effective communication to facilitate health, self- care, reasonable adjustments and shared decision-making with people;

Critically evaluate the impact of sustainable goals or targets on national public health policy and discuss the importance for delivery of health promotion and health improvement and protection in nursing;
Critique the use of digital technologies to communicate, inform, influence change, and to support role modelling and acting as ambassador for health and nursing;

Recognise common signs and symptoms of deviation from normal physiology and psychology in children, young people and adults, assessing and responding to ensure appropriate nursing care and safe administration of medicines is provided;
Critically evaluate the needs of people receiving nursing care, using self-evaluation to recognise own boundaries and professional development within the area of practice.

summative: NB: No compensation permitted. All assessment elements must be passed

data.title: LM Applied Leadership and Management
description: This module aims to enable early career nurses, midwives and allied health professionals to develop their leadership knowledge and management skills to meet the evolving aspirations of `Culture and Leadership? in the We are the NHS: People Plan (2020). This programme offers an innovative blend of leadership theory, contemporary healthcare policy, and active application to practice for new and developing clinical leaders to acquire the skills and knowledge of strategies for change management and quality service improvement, team building, networking and managing relationships.  Our multi-disciplinary approach offers a rich learning environment to build links with colleagues from other professions and services. Participants will engage with practical instances of leadership in healthcare in the real world, carry out investigative work around quality improvement and review how policy applies to local practice.

outcomes.outcome: Demonstrate a critical understanding of the use of evidence-based practice to underpin healthcare improvement.
Critically reflect upon, and use, principles of leadership, team working and change to influence improvements in person-centred care.
Demonstrate the ability to communicate, report and rationalise to a peer and professional audience the outcomes from undertaking a quality improvement project.

summative: A recorded audio PowerPoint presentation - 20 minutes (max 15 slides)
reassessment: Students will use the feedback provided to develop their work and resubmit.

description: Chronic Disease Management will appeal to clinical practitioners, from multi-professional backgrounds, working within primary or secondary care settings who have direct clinical responsibility for the assessment and management of patients presenting with chronic disease. The module will aim to develop the student's knowledge of the pathophysiology and common presenting signs and symptoms of a range of chronic diseases. Through analysis of contemporaneous national policy and clinical guidelines, the module will support the development of knowledge to facilitate the delivery of effective and comprehensive management plans to optimise patient outcome along the disease continuum.The learning and teaching approaches will be underpinned by detailed consideration of the relevant evidence base research and theory.  There will be opportunities for collaborative learning and engagement with clinicians. The module will combine lectures, workshops, seminars, and e-learning based on clinical practice that is designed in a way to enhance application of learning to the clinical environment.

outcomes.outcome: Demonstrate an integrated understanding of the altered anatomy and pathophysiology of common chronic diseases along the disease continuum.

Critically appraise and demonstrate synthesis of knowledge of the hierarchy of evidence which inform national guidelines relating to the diagnosis, treatment and monitoring of common chronic diseases.

Apply synthesis of clinical knowledge to formulate comprehensive clinical management plans for individuals living with chronic disease, with a view to promoting optimisation of self-care and management through pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions and social prescribing.

Explore social, economic and environmental factors that impact on the prevalence and distribution of common chronic diseases at a local, regional and national level with reference to public health initiatives to prevent disease.

Critically evaluate the impact of current health and social care policy on the organisational management of healthcare services for chronic disease management including engagement across the primary and secondary care interface and their influence on the patient experience (and their families) living with a chronic disease.

reassessment: Essay: students will use the feedback provided to develop their work and resubmit this

data.title: LM Clinical Assessment, Diagnostics and Decision Making
description: Module Aim

The module aims to enhance the student's knowledge,  clinical and diagnostic skills required to perform an in-depth, systematic clinical assessment across the life course as applied to the student's field of practice. This will enhance the student's ability for future risk assessment and clinical nursing decision-making.
Learning and Teaching Strategy

The module will combine recorded lectures and webinars with 30 hours demonstration and problem based learning in a simulated clinical environment. Within the laboratory students will have opportunity to observe and practice clinical and diagnostic skills related to given patient problem scenarios. Students will be provide with scenarios prior to laboratory work and in self facilitated PBL groups will develop their clinical examination skills, applying in depth knowledge of pathology, pharmokinetics and pharmacodynamics and potential diagnostic testing to their given scenario. Each lab session will include 30 minutes reflection and debrief per group.

Teaching will be led by academic staff from the Institute of Clinical Sciences, together with invited clinical lecturers, medical practitioners, visiting Advanced Practitioners and non-medical prescribers. High Fidelity simulators and patient actors (ACE's) will be used within the laboratory to develop student's clinical and diagnostic skills in a simulated environment.
Module Content

Principles of physical health assessment and diagnostics within the scope of nursing practice. Approaches to assessment using a medical systems approach including cardiovascular, neurological and respiratory assessment. Undertaking a full history, including medication history with related analysis of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. Use of ECG, microbiology and radiology and interpretation of results to inform immediate nursing decisions.
Leading and coordinating the nursing and inter-professional team in complex patient scenarios.

Delegation. Role of medical practitioners, advanced clinical practitioners and V300 non-medical prescribers. Leading urgent referral decisions and handover to medical and/or Advanced practitioners/ non-medical prescribers using a systematic approach.
Professional, legal and ethical issues, scope of practice and including application of NMC Code (2015), patient consent, confidentiality, record keeping.

outcomes.outcome: Systematically perform an age appropriate clinical assessment within their scope of nursing practice (Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE)
Critically evaluate the application of theory, clinical guidelines and research evidence informing clinical assessment and subsequent decision making  (OSCE /Reflection)
Demonstrate in depth understanding of the pathology of common disorders or diseases associated with their field of practice (OSCE)
Conduct an appropriate history and medication assessment evaluating potential effects of pharmacological interventions on patient presentation (OSCE)
Demonstrate effective teamwork to establish safe and appropriate nursing judgement and clinical decision making (OSCE).
Critically reflect upon professional role, legal and ethical issues involved in health assessment, diagnostics and clinical decision making ( OSCE/ Reflection)

summative: Group OSCE simulation of a given significant patient event within the field of practice (30 mins) and post OSCE group presentation  (15 mins ) (100%)
reassessment: There will be one further group reassessment. In the event of one student needing reassessment, a modified OSCE brief will need to be provided.

description: Consolidation of Advanced Clinical Practice: End Point Assessment is a new mandatory module within the Degree Apprenticeship Advanced Clinical Practice Apprenticeship and  Degree Apprenticeship Advanced Clinical Practice (Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy)which will encompass the recognised knowledge, skills and behaviours required to prepare advanced clinical practitioners,  within the 4 pillars of advanced clinical practice: clinical practice, leadership and management, education and research (HEE, 2017).

Practitioners will demonstrate a consolidation of learning in terms of both academic and work-based achievement throughout the course from a range of clinical specialties and health care settings. The module will facilitate the learner in integrating advanced clinical practice capabilities and specialist competencies enabling the autonomous practitioner to manage complex, person centred care within their individual scope of practice. The development and achievement of advanced clinical practice knowledge, skills and behaviours will be formally assessed through the end point assessment which will be devised in line with the Integrated Degree Apprenticeship for Advanced Clinical Practitioner at Level 7 End Point Assessment plan (Department of Education, 2018).

The assessment will deliver a valid, reliable and independent judgement that the apprentice has achieved the standard required in order to be awarded the Integrated Degree Apprenticeship for Advanced Clinical Practitioner at Level 7.

The apprentices will be prepared prior to the commencement of the Consolidation of Advanced Clinical Practice: End Point Assessment period by attending 6 days of timetabled activities to support their knowledge and understanding of the End Point Assessment process in the semester proceeding the Gateway and start of the End Point Assessment period.

outcomes.outcome: Critically reflect upon the role expectations of an advanced clinical practitioner encapsulating the capabilities supporting the 4 pillars of advanced clinical practice: clinical practice, research, leadership and management and education.

Critically evaluate the increasing level of accountability and autonomy expected of the role within the limits of their own competence, scope of practice, respective code of professional practice and governance systems.

Demonstrate the ability to manage defined and appropriate episodes of clinical care independently, from beginning to end, providing care and treatment from the time an individual first presents through to the end of the episode, which may include admission, referral or discharge or care at home, through the development of case base reflections to support the EPA open book assessment.

Demonstrate consolidation of learning from both academic and work based learning activities in order to meet the requirements of the defined knowledge, skills and behaviours which support the Level 7 Advanced Clinical Practice apprenticeship standards.

Critically appraise and synthesise the outcome of relevant research, evaluation and audit, using the results to underpin own practice and to inform that of others through dissemination of evidence based practice as part of the clinical practice change report.

reassessment: Examination and Presentation of Practice: students will use the formal verbal and written feedback provided to develop their work and be offered a resubmit

711D - MSc Nursing (Child) FT

description: The module builds on the learning in part one of the MSc Nursing and aims to enable students to advance the coordination of person-centred nursing care for people with complex, enduring conditions including people at the end of their lives. The module comprises 25% learning common to all nurses and shared learning across adult, child and mental health nursing routes and 75% of specialist field specific learning content and assessment.
Shared content:

Shared learning is coordinated by the named module leader and will address the principles and processes of safe discharge planning and the coordination of complex interdisciplinary care and use of effective communication in the interdisciplinary team. This includes building on communication skills to lead or engage in difficult and supportive conversations and decision making with service users and carers. Multi-disciplinary care co-ordination and decision making will be included. The impact of health economics on managing complex care provision, public engagement and advocacy will be debated.
Field specific content:

The module also ensures that students undertake 75% of specific learning and assessment in the context of adult or mental health or children's nursing field of practice. Students will engage with field specific learning through lectures, seminars, tutorials and practical skills classes.

Students will consider assessment and co-ordination of complex and enduring care for people relevant to their field of nursing. This will include commonly occurring enduring physical and/or mental health conditions, co-morbidities and end of life care. Consent, application of law and safeguarding related to supporting the needs of individuals, carers and families relevant to the field will be addressed.

Pharmacology and symptom management will be explored. Students will work in field specific seminar groups to research, develop and present the co-ordination of care for a person with a complex condition within their field of practice.
Field specific content, skills and assessment is co-ordinated by the field lead allocated to the module team. Reflection and debriefing activities are part of field learning.

outcomes.outcome: Discuss the co-ordination of evidence based and person centred nursing care and decision making when caring for people with complex safeguarding, enduring or end of life care needs within the field of nursing practice
Critically apply in-depth pharmacological knowledge to administration and optimisation of medicines within a field of practice
Discuss how risks to vulnerable individuals are assessed and managed in the planning and co-ordination of complex care across health and/or social care organisational boundaries
Critically evaluate legal, political and economic factors and the role of family and public engagement in the effective coordination of complex care

summative: The oral presentation will outline the continuity of care of a person with complex care needs within the student's field of nursing practice.
(50%) Coursework: Written seminar paper supporting the oral presentation (2000 words) (20.3, 20.4)
The paper will provide an in-depth analysis of a chosen aspect of complex care presented in the seminar.
No compensation permitted. Both assessments must be passed
reassessment: One further oral seminar attempt is permitted
One further attempt at written seminar paper is permitted

description: This module aims to enable students to systematically apply to person-centred care a:
Knowledge of therapeutic nursing practice to the care of adults with altered health and commonly occurring conditions;
Knowledge of pharmacology including pharmacokinetics and pharmacotherapeutics of common medications in adults and older people;

It will also facilitate the critical evaluation of person centred evidence-based therapeutic nursing care including the safe person centred transition of care for people across a care pathway and/or integrated health and social care service.
Content
Through study of problems, cases and simulated scenarios students will consider;
Effective approaches to partnership and shared clinical decision-making in evidence-based nursing practice;
Prioritisation of care, care planning and care decisions in person centred care with people, their families and carers;
Across field and multidisciplinary working, Young people care transition;
Response to deterioration or deviation from care pathways;
Safeguarding of vulnerable individuals and effectiveness of reasonable adjustments where used;
Approaches to evaluating the effectiveness of care, identifying and managing adverse events, nursing metrics and audit.

The above will include assessment, observation and therapeutic management of care in a range of settings including community, general medical and general surgical care with the need to base interventions on individual needs and preferences and the application of evidence to support and inform clinical decision-making.
Learning and Teaching

A range of learning and teaching activities will be used, including lead lectures, digital learning programmes, seminars, tutorials, case studies, digital learning, and involvement of service users, other agencies and professionals, as appropriate.

Learning and Teaching strategies will include use of lectures, digital learning and case based learning shared between adult, mental health, children's fields and including learning disability nursing with practice learning partners as relevant.  Field specific lectures, digital and case-based learning will focus on adult pathophysiology, pharmacology and therapeutic adult nursing practice.

Systematically appraise the impact of pharmacology in common medication groups on individual responses to and risks in medication as applied to a range of adults and older people;
Demonstrate health numeracy and accurately calculate medicines and prescribed drug dosages in adults;

Systematically evaluate nursing practice, utilising the evidence-base to identify effectiveness for care planning and delivery, transition and shared multi-professional decision-making along a care pathway;
Critically review factors influencing the effectiveness of continuity of care within and across organisational boundaries and identify recommendations for improvement;

Practice in accordance with the Code (NMC, 2018), undertaking delegated nursing care confidently and competently under supervision of a registered nurse or registered health/social care practitioner within a field of nursing practice;
Demonstrate the skills, behaviours and proficiencies required by part 1 of the approved practice assessment document within the adult context of nursing practice.

description: Aim:

The aim of the module is to enable the acquisition of beginning researcher skills through the planning and execution of a supervised project, together with production and presentation of the findings. For the purposes of this module, the term research project also encompasses systematic review, clinical audit, quality improvement, clinical data mining, evaluation or innovation.
Learning and Teaching:

Students will work in a group (maximum of six) to conduct a contained enquiry in response to a common problem(s) or question(s) raised by an academic supervisor and/or a partner healthcare provider or group of partner healthcare providers. Although students will work collectively as a team examining a common problem or question, students will be required to produce a final report based on the individual work they have undertaken.
Content:

Generic module content will be delivered through a variety of face to face and digital methods. Student teams will be allocated an academic supervisor with primary responsibility for the conduct of the project and liaison with other partners as appropriate. Supervisors will support, develop and supervise the project(s) and guide the student group in the development of the enquiry. Module content and supervision will include:
Ethics and governance:

Students will work in groups to consider their proposed project with regard to ethical principles and project management regarding governance of research, audit, service improvement and or evaluation.
Research Design:

Consideration of theoretical and methodological options relevant to the problem/question. Plans for data sources, data collection, data storage and analysis. Record keeping and field notes. Managing ethical, professional challenges and barriers in data collection. Planning data analysis.
Project management:

Supervisors role and responsibility. Student roles and responsibilities in the project. Teamwork and practical strategies to maintain momentum. Production of a timeline for project management including key progression / deadline dates.  Group contract signed by supervisor as required. Writing for publication. Conference dissemination, teaching presentations, intellectual property and authorship.
Data Collection:
Project implementation - ongoing review of data collection and analysis. Synthesis with existing evidence ? conclusions and recommendations.
Data Analysis:
Combination of group and individual supervision and independent working to prepare data for analysis and conduct the analysis.
Writing and Dissemination
Individual supervision will support each student in the production of their individual report and dissemination strategy.

outcomes.outcome: Articulate the theoretical, methodological and ethical/governance dimensions of a health and/or social care enquiry project;
Systematically analyse, interpret and present results of an enquiry-based project;
Critically evaluate the implications of project findings for health and/or social care practice, delivery, education or further enquiry (Report);
Work effectively within a team to plan, execute and communicate project findings.

summative: (20%) group conference style poster, or presentation (group mark awarded - students who cannot attend a presentation due to extenuating circumstances will be given a viva voce (18.4).
reassessment: Students will resubmit any failed component(s);
Report: resubmit following feedback, support and guidance;
Poster or presentation: resubmit following feedback, support and guidance. Students who cannot attend a presentation due to extenuating circumstances will be given a viva voce.
No compensation permitted. All assessment elements must be passed

data.title: LM Leadership and Management in Health Care
description: The importance of leadership in bringing about change to improve health and well-being is recognised, however leadership in health requires participation of staff, patients and the public if it is to be inclusive and effective.  The management responsibilities of healthcare leaders also need to be taken into account.  Moreover leadership in health care is concerned with both outcomes (improved health) and values (equity in health outcomes, appropriateness of services/care).  This module will enable students to examine health care leadership and management and apply it to a range of contexts.It will involve critical analysis of relevant theories and research, along with focussed discussion of the application of principles and methods in different health care settings.

outcomes.outcome: Examine critically a range of theories and models of leadership and management in health care
Analyse critically the effectiveness of particular  management and leadership styles as applied in different cultures, contexts, and health services
Discuss critically the application of a range of strategies to harness the potential of teams in healthcare organisations
Evaluate the impact of the organisational and policy context on leadership in health care

Teaching and Learning Strategy:

This module utilises a flipped learning approach, where students are introduced to material prior to the session, which allows deeper understanding to develop from discussion and activities in class. This pedagogical approach will help to foster critical thinking and questioning skills whilst building essential `scaffolding? for students to develop throughout the module and their nursing career .

Clinical placements are undertaken as part of this module. Students are expected to demonstrate their ability and competence to lead and manage teams in organising and prioritising care. By the end of the final placement for the/each field of practice they must demonstrate that they are safe and competent to make the transition from student to NMC registered nurse in that field and have met all current NMC standards and proficiencies and be in compliance with the NMC Code (2018).

Students will collect evidence of facilitating learning opportunities for others within or related to the clinical environment including the assessment of competence for delegated activities. This evidence will be presented in an e-portfolio as part of the module assessment strategy.

description: Maternal and Child Mental Health is 20 credit bearing optional module within the MSc Advanced Clinical Practice (ACP) and MSc Advanced Heath Care Practice ( Global) programmes, which will also facilitate the multi-professional requirements for the Apprenticeship Standards for Advanced Clinical Practice (2018) (HEE, 2017). The module will promote student's learning about maternal and child mental health to support best practice in three key domains:

1. Improving assessment skills to identify and respond to mental and physical needs at the clinical interface with health and social care (Five Year Forward Review 2014; Leading Change, Adding Value, 2016);
2. Developing collaborative approaches to ensure optimum antenatal and postnatal mental health for women and  children (NICE, 2016);
3. Reducing the risk of lifelong harms associated with poor social and emotional wellbeing of children in the early years (NICE, 2012).

It is anticipated that the learning will help students achieve generalist capabilities outlined within the 4 pillars for advanced clinical practice (clinical practice, research, leadership and management and education) combined with the specialist theoretical underpinnings of maternal and child mental health, which will be delivered by clinically informed Masters level preparation. The learning and teaching approaches will be underpinned by detailed consideration of the relevant evidence base research and theory.  There will be opportunities for collaborative learning and engagement with clinicians. The module will combine lectures, workshops, seminars, and e-learning based on clinical practice that is designed in a way to enhance application of learning to the clinical environment.

outcomes.outcome: Demonstrate synthesis and application of theories about the relationship between maternal and child mental health, acquired from relevant clinical and operational guidance and the wider research literature.

Critically reflect upon health assessment activities, which have informed practitioner identification and response to the incidence and prevalence of maternal and child mental illness across the life-course.

Evidence the risk factors associated with poor maternal and child mental health, reflecting upon specialist roles and collaborative capacity to improve mental health and wellbeing outcomes for vulnerable populations.
Identify asset-based approaches to maternal and child mental health promotion, considering how to improve service user involvement and engagement with mental health interventions.

reassessment: Essay: students will use the feedback provided to develop their work and resubmit this

optional: 319I - PG Aff Pra Cer In Pr (NMC ACP)
584B - MSc Advanced Clinical Pract PT

description: The module enables students to synthesise underpinning principles and apply these to developing simulated independent prescribing practice drawing upon appropriate clinical assessment, diagnosis and management of prescribing decisions including effective communication. Students will extend their use of appropriate diagnostic skills and decision making as part of simulated and immersive learning. Learning strategies in theory and practice are designed to develop a critical, personalised approach towards safe and effective prescribing using appropriate problem-solving and recognising boundaries. Their practice will be based on the recognition and application of appropriate national or local therapeutic guidelines and governance.
This module is designed to be:

(1) Co-requisite with the modules Prescribing: Scientific Principles and Practice (Module 1) and Prescribing: Structured Reflective Portfolio (Module 3) to meet the requirements for an accredited programme for independent non-medical prescriber status (according to each relevant professional body, GPhC, NMC, HCPC).

(2) a self-standing CPD module to provide extended knowledge and understanding of the medical prescribing process (to service existing prescribers wishing to develop their knowledge base or those who do not necessarily prescribe but are involved with a medicines management process).

outcomes.outcome: Demonstrate the ability to communicate effectively with patients or carers to gain an accurate patient history with a patient-centred approach to shared decision-making that considers all treatment, management and support options including social prescribing or a decision not to prescribe.  Demonstrated through lectures, workshops; assessed with case based - discussions, significant event analysis, OSCEs

Demonstrate the process of differential diagnostic decision-making based on a range of commonly occurring signs and symptoms including relevant clinical assessment, appropriate use of common diagnostic equipment and identification of red flags.  Demonstrated through workshops; assessed wit, significant event analysis with clinical management, DPP assessment, OSCE

Make an independent formulation of an accurate working diagnosis and safe simulated independent prescribing decision, including clinical assessment, monitoring, safety checks and follow up, recognising and responding appropriately to factors that may influence prescribing.  Demonstrated through workshops; assessed with significant event analysis with clinical management, DPP assessment, OSCE

Critically analyse potential and simulated independent prescribing decisions, appraising options, drawing on a systematic review of evidence based sources which are accessed and utilised to support safe and effective prescribing practice.  Demonstrated through workshops; assessed with case-based discussion, significant event analysis with clinical management, DPP assessment

Develop an appropriate clinical management plan, generating accurate prescriptions if appropriate with effective and timely record-keeping, demonstrating the ability to distinguish between independent and supplementary prescribing.  Demonstrated through workshops; assessed with significant event analysis with clinical management, DPP assessment

Appraise the role of the multi-disciplinary team in ensuring continuity of care and safe, effective independent prescribing decisions.  Demonstrated through workshops; assessed with significant event analysis with clinical management, DPP assessment

Demonstrate ability to practice within the limits of professional competence (including appropriate referral, consultation and guidance seeking).  Demonstrated though workshops; assessed with significant event analysis with clinical management DPP assessment, OSC

Critical application of public health, legal, ethical, professional, audit and governance frameworks in the prescribing process.  Demonstrated through workshops; assessed with significant event analysis with clinical management, DPP assessment, OSCE

Critically reflect on personal prescribing practice referring to RPS (2021) Competency Framework for all Prescribers, professional regulatory guidance and codes of practice to demonstrate an understanding of the accountability and responsibility that prescribing entails with critical awareness of personal limitations.  Demonstrated through workshops; assessed with significant event analysis with clinical management, DPP assessment, OSCE

summative: All assessments are held in accordance with the General regulations for Postgraduate Programmes.

In any assessment, a failure to identify a serious problem or an answer which would cause the patient harm will result in overall failure of the module.  Re-application to the module will be considered on a `case by case? basis.
If the module is being taken as part of the Practice Certificate in Independent Prescribing this would mean an overall failure of the programme.
1. Three station OSCE examination - 3 manned stations
Pass/Fail required component (0% of module mark) (50% pass mark)
Failure of any OSCE station will require the student to re-sit the OSCE component of the module.

All assessment components must be passed at the required pass mark to pass the module.
Compensation of individual components is not available.
reassessment: If a student fails any component of the module (excluding the required component), then on successful completion the final result will be capped at 50% for the module as a whole.
Students will have one re-assessment attempt at each element.

description: The module is designed to introduce the student to the underpinning theoretical principles supporting safe and effective independent prescribing practice. Students will revise pathophysiology of key body systems and apply principles of clinical assessment including the signs, symptoms and red flags that inform diagnostic decision making. Common diagnostic tests will be discussed. The fundamentals of pharmacology, drug interactions (pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics) will be explored, underpinned with mandated independent learning from Script online modules. Students will learn the legal, regulatory framework and principles of governance required for safe prescribing practice. This will include accessing and using the evidence base accurately and safely to optimise the prescribing process at patient, local practice and national levels. Students will be developing a critical appreciation of the influences on and psychology associated with the prescribing process. They will be able to critically assess the complex contexts in which the prescribing process is conducted and be able to respond dynamically with appropriate prescribing actions. They will build a critical knowledge base of the principles of evidence-based practice and clinical governance for complex, multi-factorial prescribing scenarios. Students will be developing application of prescribing principles on their own intended area of prescribing and starting to develop their structured learning and reflection portfolio as part of module 3 Prescribing: Structured Reflective Portfolio.
This module is designed to be:

(1) Co-requisite with the modules Prescribing: Safe Effective Practice and Prescribing: Structured Reflective Portfolio to meet the requirements for an accredited programme for independent non-medical prescriber status (according to each relevant professional body, GPhC, NMC, HCPC).

(2) a self-standing CPD module to provide extended knowledge and understanding of the medical prescribing process (to service existing prescribers wishing to develop their knowledge base or those who do not necessarily prescribe but are involved with a medicines management process).

description: This is a non-credit bearing module undertaken as a mandatory component of the Practice Certificate in Independent Prescribing. The module aims to facilitate fulfilment of the practice component of a programme leading to eligibility to record an independent prescribing qualification with the student's relevant professional, regulatory body. Profession specific learning and requirements for this module are stipulated in a professional structured reflective portfolio handbook, which includes evidence of ongoing supervised learning records, academic and practice assessment and achievement.

The module will provide opportunity for students to reflect on the integration of theory to their scope of practice. Profession focused study days which, depending on the group and activity, may be timetabled as face to face or as a digital activity to introduce and support them in their portfolio development. The learning and teaching approaches are designed to be reflective and action based and will facilitate the compilation of robust evidence to support their developing prescribing practice.

description: Clinical Decision Making is a process that leads to effective and evidence-based actions. This is a fundamental skill required for Masters level advanced practice where the ability to make sound judgements, interpolate missing information, and manage risk in complex clinical contexts are an expectation. This module aims to develop the student's knowledge of clinical decision-making theory and apply this their area of practice. To accomplish this students will explore assessment models and principles, a range of assessment tools, theoretical approaches to diagnostic reasoning, and the principles of critical analysis and reflection applied to their clinical practice. At the end of the module the student will have advanced their mastery of problem-focused clinical decision making that demonstrates safe and effective service delivery. They will be able demonstrate their ability to analyse, integrate and synthesise information derived from their practice and using a critical and reflexive approach to illustrate their decision making for peer and academic review

outcomes.outcome: By the end of the Module, students should be able to:

Identify and evaluate advanced concepts underlying theoretical assessment frameworks and the use of a range of assessment methods to communicate your findings and to support your judgments and potential interventions.
Critically appraise, summarise and incorporate into the decision-making process relevant policy and theory relating to public health, epidemiology, and/or health promotion.
Select, critically evaluate and integrate research, professional, legal and ethical considerations that  impact on clinical decision making in own area of practice and the wider health care economy.

Critically evaluate and justify decision making in the light of healthcare outcomes, incorporating patients/service user and/or family/carer perspectives within the context of available health care resources.

description: The aim of this module is to introduce students to quantitative research design, data collection and analysis, so that they can confidently appraise quantitative research and use quantitative skills in their own research projects.

The module introduces students to primary quantitative research methods that are commonly used within applied health research (cohort studies, case control and randomised controlled trials). Students will develop the necessary skills to formulate research ideas and identify appropriate methods to test a hypothesis. Quantitative research design, sampling strategies, data collection and data analysis techniques involved in quantitative research are explored to enable students to identify common sources of bias and misreporting. The module also provides an introduction to computer software (SPSS/Excel) to manage and analyse data.

outcomes.outcome: Apply and critically evaluate structured frameworks (e.g., PICO, PEO, SPIDER) to formulate clear, focused, and researchable questions that align with complex clinical, professional, or theoretical issues.
Design and justify a methodologically sound research strategy, selecting an appropriate quantitative in alignment with the research aim.
Interrogate ethical principles and governance frameworks to evaluate the ethical implications of proposed research, demonstrating advanced ethical reasoning and reflexivity.
Critically evaluate and select appropriate data collection methods, demonstrating the ability to manage practical, theoretical, and contextual challenges in research implementation.

Critically analyse and interpret descriptive and inferential statistical data, including the application of hypothesis testing, applying advanced reasoning to draw valid conclusions and inform evidence-based practice or policy.

summative: Part A: Analysis of data set (40%)
Part B: 20 minute + 10 minute Q&A recorded powerpoint presentation of research study protocol incorporating question formulation, research design, ethical considerations and data collection (60%)
Students must pass both elements of the assignment at 50% or more in order to pass the module
reassessment: Students will have to undertake any of the elements they failed at first attempt

data.title: LM Recognising and responding to acute deterioration within complex adult nursing care. (RAR7)

comp: 699D - MNurs (Adult) FT

description: The module aims to enhance the student's knowledge, clinical and diagnostic skills required to perform an in-depth, systematic clinical assessment to safely respond to deteriorating patients. Students will interpret a range of results to formulate a defendable condition hypothesis (working diagnosis). Furthermore, students will critically analyse the potential effects of comorbidities and pharmacology on acutely ill service users. Using these results students will independently articulate clinical management decisions developing an appropriate plan of adult nursing care including safe delegation or referral to medical staff or other appropriate professionals. This will enhance the student's clinical decision-making for individuals requiring acute complex care.

The module will develop knowledge of prescribing legislation, and application of detailed pharmacological knowledge to adult nursing. Bioscience concepts will be developed as a core component to support students with their recognition of deterioration and clinical decision-making.

A range of learning and teaching activities will be used, including case studies, lead lectures, group work seminars, and skills and simulation teaching, supported by digital learning and engagement with service users, other agencies, and professionals, as appropriate. Any outstanding communication and management skills or nursing procedures will be assessed through simulation during this module with the involvement of appropriate practice assessors.

outcomes.outcome: Systematically perform an evidence-based clinical assessment rationalising an in-depth understanding of the underpinning evidence to produce a condition hypothesis with service users related to adult nursing practice.
Critically apply theory to prioritise and rationalise appropriate care interventions, in order to independently plan, share information, manage, and delegate adult nursing care.

Critically evaluate clinical guidelines and research evidence to conduct an appropriate medication assessment, articulating safe prescribing principles and the potential effects of a pharmacological intervention on patient presentation.

Synthesise bioscience knowledge to critically analyse and evaluate clinical information in order to recognise physiological deterioration in a service user with comorbidities and acute complex conditions.
Critically discuss the ethical, legal, and professional issues that underpin decision-making when caring for the acutely ill service user.
Evaluate nursing cultural and organisational factors that influence the care of service users with complex health needs.

reassessment: Students will re-sit or resubmit any failed component(s)

data.title: LM Research and Improvement Methods for Practice
description: Healthcare students must engage with different forms of inquiry (research, audit, improvement, and evaluation) to help them understand, improve and innovate in practice.  In this module they will be exposed to different types of evidence gathering strategies and data analysis techniques that can be used to explore, understand, or evaluate aspects of care, service delivery or experience of health and illness.

The students will critically examine the relationship between, audit, research, and evaluation to drive improvement. They will gain a critical understanding of the principles of clinical governance, audit, quality improvement and the underpinning ethical governance. They will understand the contribution that public, patient participation, involvement and engagement can make to research and improvement science.

Students will complete the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) e-learning programme Introduction to Good Clinical Practice (GCP). This is a compulsory requirement for the module and requires certificated evidence of completion to pass the module.

outcomes.outcome: Evaluate the benefits and challenges associated with planning and conducting research, audit, quality improvement and service redesign in health and social care
Apply the principles of clinical governance and, ethical conduct to research, audit or quality improvement
Appraise research evidence and improvement designs employed to enhance safety, care and experience of people using or delivering health and social care services
Examine the contribution of public and patient participation involvement and engagement in improving health and social care
Consider barriers that can impact on research transfer, and knowledge utilisation, spread and improvement science

summative: 100% Open book examination, short answer.                 2 hours (100%),
0% NIHR GCP E-Learning Certificate          Pass/FailInternal hurdle
reassessment: Students will be permitted one re-sit or resubmit of any failed component(s).

description: The Research Dissertation will demonstrate students? consolidation and application of advanced practice and research knowledge and skills by undertaking a research task relevant to the students? current area of practice. It will build upon the proposal submitted for Creating and Applying Evidence (pre-requisite).
Students will undertake a research investigation under the guidance of a supervisor after determining an appropriate methodology for the inquiry task, and subject to module lead approval.

The investigation could take the form of a systematic review or thematic synthesis or project involving fi fieldwork (subject to appropriate ethical and/or governance requirements). Outcomes of the study will be contextualised in terms of clinical significance and potential for transformation of services, or care delivery, or improving patient care or healthcare professional  education or policy.

outcomes.outcome: By the end of the Module, students should be able to:
Construct and implement a plan of inquiry relevant to the clinical area, research unit or educational institution pertaining to health and/or social care.
Critically analyse and evaluate literature and current policy in the chosen are of practice to determine and refine and inform the focus of research inquiry.

Distinguish appropriate methods of investigation for the research task; providing convincing rationale for the study, justifying the relevance to the field of practice, and recognising potential  limitations and challenges.
Collect, categorise and critically analyse data or information/data relevant to the subject.

Integrate and synthesise thethe data collected and explain the significance, clinical relevance, and implications for service transformation for patient, population or professional, service delivery benefit.

summative: Word count: 10,000 (+/- 10%) words.  The student must achieve an overall mark of at least 50%.

and will introduce learners to the concepts associated with midwifery continuity of care(r) and working as a colleague and leader. description: The Reflective Advanced Practitioner is a mandatory module within the MSc Advanced Clinical Practice which will encompass the requirements for advanced clinical practice outlined within the 4 pillars: clinical practice, leadership and management, education and research (HEE, 2017).

The module will examine critical thinking and reflective practice in the context of the 4 pillars, with emphasis on the development of clinical leadership skills within these domains to fulfil the role requirements of effective advanced clinical practitioners. The learning and teaching approaches will be underpinned by detailed consideration of the relevant research and theory.  There will be opportunities for collaborative learning and engagement with clinical leaders and researchers.

outcomes.outcome: Critically evaluate the role expectations of an advanced clinical practitioner with respect to the 4 pillars of advanced clinical practice: clinical practice, research, leadership and management and education. Critically reflect upon their developing role and personal developmental needs in line with these role expectations.

Demonstrate a critical understanding of an advanced clinical practitioner's broadened level of responsibility and autonomy and the limits of own competence and professional scope of practice in line with their respective code of professional conduct and governance systems.

Critically evaluate theories and models of clinical leadership, service development and risk management whilst demonstrating an in-depth understanding of the processes required to successfully drive change within health care organisations.

Demonstrate an in-depth understanding of the importance of communication and collaborative working in leading advanced clinical practice with respect to the 4 pillars of advanced clinical practice: clinical practice, research, leadership and management and education.

Demonstrate the ability to critically appraise and synthesise the outcome of relevant research, evaluation and audit, using the results to underpin own practice and to inform that of others through dissemination of evidence based practice.

data.title: LM Transforming healthcare and service design
description: Healthcare organisations are highly complex contexts facing particular challenges Most healthcare systems have adopted improving population health, enhancing the experience of patients, cost containment and the wellbeing of the healthcare workforce as key aims.

This module critically explores contemporary health care systems through the lens of innovation, safety and transformation. Students will be encouraged to critically appraise challenges they encounter in delivery of care; examine the tension and dissonance between policy and real world delivery; explore the salience of clinical and corporate governance; examine patient and public involvement and engagement, factors influencing organisational change and strategies and approaches to critically appraise and transform care, services, systems and workforce wellbeing.

outcomes.outcome: Critically appraise healthcare policy, systems and models of delivery
Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of improvement theories, methodologies, methods and application to transform healthcare
Judge the effectiveness of clinical and corporate governance structures and demonstrate a critical awareness of current challenges and offer novel insights
Investigate, propose and critique strategies used to influence organisational, service or system change in healthcare including patient and public involvement and engagement

description: This module aligns to NMC (2019) Standards of Proficiency for Midwives
Domain 3

and will introduce students to key concepts, policy and practice related to universal midwifery care.  Exploring how universal care impacts on the life course of women, other childbearing people and newborn infants and how working in partnership can optimise positive outcomes, to include identifying and preventing complications, learners will examine the homogeneity and diversity of women and other childbearing people's lived experiences and the resources and opportunities available to them, to include the impact of inequalities and the role of the midwife in enhancing population health. Learners will develop knowledge and understanding of anatomy, physiology, genetics, genomics and medicines related to childbearing, the sexual and reproductive health of adolescent girls and women, fetal development, neonatal adaptation and infant feeding. Opportunities to continue to develop academic study, leadership, research and teamwork skills will be provided through the use of Enquiry Based Learning.

Critically analyse ethical, legal, political and professional issues, and other factors that positively and negatively influence the health and wellbeing outcomes of women, other childbearing people, and their newborn infants accessing universal care

Engage in the development of relevant questions and the location, critical appraisal and application of appropriate evidence sources to inform personal knowledge acquisition and that of the wider midwifery community of practice
Develop an evidence-based digital resource to support women, other childbearing people, and their families to achieve positive outcomes when accessing universal care
